what_is_checked: create: null-vs-object gate on the type byte; field values (options blob, format_version, max_output_len)
reset: stored input buffer zeroed; a post-reset compress emits a fresh frame that one-shot-decompresses to the input alone

compress: empty input returns 0; same-object continuation finishes the frame; a new object restarts it; the same-object-new-size quirk (old size governs); every produced frame carries the checksum flag and one-shot-decompresses to exactly the input
uncompress: whole-frame, nullptr-continuation after a full output buffer, re-passed-input restart, empty input, garbage/corrupt frames -> -1 with the buffer reset
error branches: the engine passthroughs stubbed to return a ZSTD error code assert Reset + return -1

task_question: How do node #115's RocksDB ZSTD streaming compress/uncompress wrappers work: the two Create factories, the Compress/Uncompress streaming calls, and the two Resets?
unknowns: The 48-byte CompressionOptions layout: the factory copies it opaquely and no field is consumed by the factory or the ctor (only checksumFlag is set on the CCtx), so the field boundaries are not pinned here.

The destructors ZSTDStreamingCompress::~ZSTDStreamingCompress (frees the CCtx) and ZSTDStreamingUncompress::~ZSTDStreamingUncompress (frees the DCtx) are separate FDEs (uncompress D1 0x5f01520 / D0 0x5f014f0 per the vtable packet) and are NOT reconstructed in this packet; the tool's close() is the Python-side analogue, not a binary claim.

The enclosing functions of the two factory callers (FDE 0x5f041d0 and FDE 0x5f01e80) are not identified beyond their observed argument setup; only the call sites and the installed products are claimed.

The exact ZSTD error code returned by the stubbed error branches is the generic -70 used by the test stub; the binary's error path triggers on whatever code the engine returns, and the wrapper's response (Reset + -1) does not depend on the code value.

The system libzstd used as the engine oracle is 1.5.5; the target statically links zstd 1.5.7. Streaming frame format and API semantics are stable across these versions; frame bytes are not claimed identical.

notes: StreamingCompress::Create(type, opts, uint32_t compress_format_version, size_t max_output_len); only kZSTD (7) builds an object, others return nullptr.
StreamingUncompress::Create(type, uint32_t compress_format_version, size_t max_output_len); same gate.
ZSTDStreamingCompress ctor: cctx_ = ZSTD_createCCtx(); ZSTD_CCtx_setParameter(cctx_, ZSTD_c_checksumFlag, 1); input_buffer_ = {nullptr, 0, 0}. No compression level is applied.
The source's ZSTD_Streaming_Supported() check in both factories has no call in the binary: it folds away with ZSTD_STREAMING defined (zstd >= 1.4.0).
Compress/Uncompress/Reset bodies in util/compression.cc match the binary instruction-for-instruction in structure, including the early returns and the error paths.
